title: Parseval's identity for the Walsh–Fourier expansion
statement:
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean hypercube, and for each subset $S \subseteq [n]$ let $\hat f(S) = \langle f, \chi_S\rangle$ be its Fourier coefficient, where the inner product and expectation are taken with respect to the uniform measure. Then the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients equals the squared $L^2$ norm of $f$:
\[
  \sum_{S \subseteq [n]} \hat f(S)^2 \;=\; \|f\|_2^2 \;=\; \E\bigl[f^2\bigr].
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a real-valued function on the Boolean hypercube {0,1}^n
